title: Mark as Billable prices the line as a new line would be
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, with its own labor rate of $120.00 an hour.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in status Approved, billable, with line 1 of 2.0 hours at $120.00 an hour and line 2 of 1.5 hours with one stock part costing $40.00, line 2 marked No Charge under Goodwill.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open line 2's three-dots menu.
  3. Click "Mark as Billable".
  4. Click the confirming Mark as Billable button.
  5. Open the Notes tab.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The menu shows "Mark as Billable".

Step 3:

  • A window titled "Mark line as billable?" reads "The line is priced as a new line would be today. You can mark it No Charge again until the work order is invoiced."
  • Its buttons are "Cancel" and "Mark as Billable".

Step 4:

  • The chip is gone.
  • Line 2's labor reads $180.00 (1.5 h × $120.00) and its part is priced by the pricing rules from its $40.00 cost.

Step 5:

  • A note reads "Line '[line 2's title]' marked Billable by [user]. Priced as a new line would be today: $[price]. Category Goodwill removed."

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-12226 (Story 12, A no-charge line on a billable work order)

  • S12-R5: “The three-dots menu of a no-charge line offers "Change category" (the dialog of S12-R2 with the current values; Save is enabled once the category, the original work order or the original line differs) and "Mark as Billable" (confirmation "Mark line as billable?" with the body "The line is priced as a new line would be today. You can mark it No Charge again until the work order is invoiced."); confirming removes the chip and the category and prices the line as S2-R6 prices a line: labor at the customer's rate, else the location's; parts from the pricing rules on the cost already on the line. Both are unavailable once the work order is invoiced; the invoice is reversed first, as for Convert (S2-R9).”
  • S12-R6: “Each action writes a system note on the work order and an Audit Log row (S2-R18): "Line '[title]' marked No Charge by [user]. Category [name], original work order [number], original line [number]. Line price $[price] removed; cost $[cost] and [hours] h kept. The work order stays billable."; "Category of line '[title]' changed from [a] to [b] by [user]."; "Line '[title]' marked Billable by [user]. Priced as a new line would be today: $[price]. Category [name] removed."”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Mark as Billable (line menu) | "Mark line as billable?" with the body "The line is priced as a new line would be today. You can mark it No Charge again until the work order is invoiced." | Confirmation, Cancel / Mark as Billable (S12-R5)”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Line marked, category changed, line made billable | The three notes of S12-R6 | System note on the work order and Audit Log row”
